native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignifcant) when both race and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: Socioeconomic status (SES). The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from roughly +0.36 in a simple regression to about -0.23 and becomes statistically insignificant when race and academic characteristics (ASVAB composite ability score and class percentile) are included simultaneously in the model, consistent with mediation: most of the SES->BA association runs indirectly through academic resources at secondary-school exit (ability and class rank), with a smaller contribution from confounding by race; once race and academic characteristics are held constant, SES shows no positive direct association with completing a BA. Caveat: observational/cross-sectional data, highly imbalanced outcome (~2.7% BA completion), and the adjusted SES coefficient is borderline at the 5% level (p~0.02; insignificant at the 1% level).
